title: Prefill Throttler and Tenant-Isolation for Continuous Batching
creator: Harini Rao
description:
Problem: tail latency and noisy-tenant interference in continuous batching are causing p99 spikes for interactive hosted API customers. Prefill-heavy workloads from a few tenants saturate batch slots and force kernel choices that are suboptimal for short decode requests, worsening p95/p99. Goal: implement a prefill-throttler with tenant-aware fair-queueing and admission shaping to reduce long-tail latency while preserving throughput and utilization.

Scope: implement admission layer changes in the serving runtime admission controller, a prefill token budget per-tenant, decode-time shaping heuristics, and a small kernel-selection signal so the scheduler prefers low-latency kernels when decode-dominant requests are held back. This ticket covers design, prototype, benchmarks, and canary rollout for hosted API.

High-level approach: 1) Introduce a lightweight per-tenant credit bucket (prefill budget) that drains on prefill admission and replenishes at a configured rate; 2) Add a fair-queueing admission discipline that isolates tenants that exceed burst budget and schedules their requests into a low-priority pool; 3) Implement decode-time throttler that dynamically reduces admission for long-prefill requests when tail latencies exceed SLO thresholds; 4) Expose kernel-selection hint from admission controller to the kernel scheduler: "latency_biased" vs "throughput_biased" so the runtime can pick optimized kernels for short-decode flows; 5) Add metrics, dashboards, and an experiment framework to validate trade-offs.

Trade-offs considered: lowering admission for heavy prefill tenants can reduce aggregate throughput and utilization; we will use adaptive replenishment to allow graceful bursts. Kernel hints are advisory — strict coupling with kernel-selection risks oscillation, so we prefer soft signals with smoothing. We will prioritize correctness/availability over aggressive latency clipping (no request drops in first iteration).
acceptance_criteria: 1) p99 latency for interactive small-decode workloads decreases by >= 30% under mixed workload tests; 2) overall token throughput degradation <= 8% in benchmark mix; 3) new metrics (per-tenant prefill_budget, prefill_throttle_rate, admission_queue_length) are emitted; 4) canary rollout on 5% traffic without customer-visible errors for 48h; 5) runbook updated and on-call trained.
comments: 2026-02-28 Harini Rao: Created ticket after incident analysis (INC-2026-02-26) showed tenant burst correlation with p99 spikes. Added initial goals and KPIs.

2026-03-02 Miguel Ortega: Spike meeting notes: prefer per-tenant credit approach vs strict token caps. Decided to prototype with token-bucket replenishment (configurable rate) and a low-priority backlog for throttled requests.

2026-03-04 Design review (Lina Chen): Request that the admission controller expose a maturity flag before kernel hinting reaches the long-term scheduler — avoid premature coupling. Action: add smoothing window and observability for kernel-hint toggles.

2026-03-06 Engineering update (Miguel Ortega): Prototype implemented in branch feature/prefill-throttler. Baseline microbenchmarks show p99 reduction for short-decode flows but 10% throughput drop under synthetic prefill-heavy mix. Next: tune replenish rate and backlog scheduling policy.

2026-03-08 Perf results (bench-run-20260308): With replenish_rate=200 tokens/s and backlog_priority=low we see p99 improve 38% for chat-like flows, throughput drop reduced to 6%. Added new Grafana panels for prefill_budget and backlog queue length.

2026-03-09 QA notes (Anita Gupta): Found a deadlock when tenant backlog exceeds 1000 pending prefill items during a prolonged outage simulation. Root cause: backlog consumer stalled when kernel-scheduler delayed due to memory pressure. Mitigation: cap backlog drain concurrency and add backpressure to prefill admission.

2026-03-11 Miguel Ortega: Adjusted design: add backlog_concurrency_limit, backlog_age_eviction (30s), and telemetry for evicted requests (should be rare). Updated PRs: #3456, #3472. Added canary plan for 5% traffic in us-west-2.

2026-03-12 PM feedback (Devon Park): Ensure SLA owners (enterprise customers) are notified about behavior changes and allow per-customer opt-out toggles for initial canary. Action: add opt-out flag per-tenant and plan communications.
2026-03-12 Harini Rao: Updated acceptance criteria and rollout checklist. Scheduling a rollout rehearsal on 2026-03-18 with on-call and SRE.
2026-03-12 Miguel Ortega: Next steps: finalize config API for per-tenant budgets, complete integration tests for kernel-hint smoothing, and prepare canary runbook.
